info.title: Presend API
info.description: Free security & verification API -- 24 endpoints for supply-chain, web, and file security checks. No signup, no API key.

post.description: Returns SHA-256, SHA-1 and SHA-512 for a file up to 20MB.

post.summary: Detect real file type from binary signature
post.description: Detects a file's real type from its binary signature ("magic bytes"), and flags a mismatch against the claimed Content-Type -- catches disguised files that slip past naive upload filters.

example.warning: Claimed type "image/jpeg" does not match the file's actual signature (detected: "image/png"). This can indicate a disguised or mislabeled file.

post.summary: Hash a file and check it against known malware
post.description: Computes SHA-256 and checks it against MalwareBazaar (abuse.ch), a free database of confirmed malware samples. Only catches already-known samples -- a 'not found' result does not guarantee the file is safe.

example.verdict: Not found in MalwareBazaar. This does not guarantee the file is safe — only that this exact file is not currently known to this database.

get.description: Decodes the header and payload of a JWT. Does not verify the signature.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The JWT to decode. Decodes header and payload only -- does not verify the signature (use /jwt-verify for that).

post.description: Actually verifies the signature (HS256/384/512, RS/PS256/384/512, ES256/384/512) via the Workers-native Web Crypto API, plus exp/nbf claim checks. Unlike /jwt-decode, this performs real cryptographic verification.

token.description: The JWT to verify. Checks the cryptographic signature -- use /jwt-decode if you only need to read the header and payload.

jwk.description: Public key in JWK format, for RS/PS/ES algorithms.

jwks_url.description: URL to a JWKS document; the key is matched by the token's "kid" header.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Desired password length. Defaults to a reasonable secure length if omitted.

parameters.name: symbols
parameters.description: Whether to include symbol characters. 1 for yes, 0 for no.

parameters.name: uppercase
parameters.description: Whether to include uppercase letters. 1 for yes, 0 for no.

parameters.name: numbers
parameters.description: Whether to include numeric digits. 1 for yes, 0 for no.

parameters.name: exclude_ambiguous
parameters.description: Whether to exclude visually ambiguous characters (e.g. 0/O, 1/l). 1 for yes, 0 for no.

get.summary: Check if a password has been breached
get.description: Uses HIBP k-anonymity — only 5 hash chars are sent externally.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password to check against known data-breach corpora. Only a 5-character SHA-1 hash prefix is sent to HIBP (k-anonymity), but the password itself travels in this request's URL; for real passwords, prefer the password-check endpoint (POST body).

post.description: Chains entropy/strength scoring with an optional HIBP breach check in a single call. Password is sent in the JSON body, never in a URL.

password.description: Password to evaluate for strength (length, character variety, common patterns).

check_breach.description: Whether to also check the password against known data-breach corpora via k-anonymity. true or false.

200.description: Strength analysis and optional breach result

get.description: Checks SPF strength, DMARC policy, and a best-effort DKIM lookup against common selectors. DKIM has no fixed DNS location, so absence of a match does not prove DKIM is unconfigured.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain to check SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records for, e.g. example.com.

dkim.note: Best-effort: only common selectors are tested. A domain can have valid DKIM under a custom selector not listed here — absence of a match does not prove DKIM is unconfigured.

get.description: Combines security-headers, url-reputation, and subdomains into a single overall score and verdict, run in parallel.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: URL to run a combined security posture check against (headers, reputation, and related signals).

post.summary: Decode a QR code and check its URL reputation
post.description: Decodes a QR code from an uploaded JPEG/PNG image. If the content is a URL, checks it against URLhaus for malware/phishing indicators in the same call. QR-code phishing ("quishing") is one of the fastest-growing phishing vectors, bypassing text-based filters.

200.description: Decoded content and, if applicable, reputation check

example.verdict: QR code links to a URL not currently flagged by URLhaus. This does not guarantee safety — only that it is not currently listed.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: URL to audit HTTP security headers for (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, etc.).

get.summary: Check which AI crawlers are allowed by robots.txt
get.description: Fetches robots.txt and reports which known AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, etc.) are allowed or blocked. Free, no signup required.

lodash vulnerable to Prototype Pollution via array path bypass in `_.unset` and `_.omit`

post.description: Checks up to 100 package names in one request, counted as a single request for rate limiting. Same analysis as GET; an invalid entry yields {package, error} instead of failing the batch.

results.description: One entry per input name, in input order. Same fields as the GET response, or {package, error} for an invalid entry.

400.description: Invalid JSON body, unsupported ecosystem, empty list, or more than 100 names

get.description: Flags package names that are a near-miss of a curated list of well-known npm/PyPI packages (Damerau-Levenshtein: 1 edit for 4-7 character names, 2 for 8+; names of 3 characters or fewer are not fuzzy-matched) -- the classic typosquatting pattern. A batch POST variant is available.

parameters.name: ecosystem
parameters.description: Package ecosystem, e.g. npm or PyPI.

parameters.name: package
parameters.description: Package name to check for likely typosquatting of a well-known package in the given ecosystem.

200.description: Typosquatting analysis for the package name

known_legitimate.description: True when the name resembles a well-known package but is itself a manually reviewed legitimate package (e.g. preact vs react, psycopg vs psycopg2). Such names are not flagged as suspicious.

example.note: Name is within edit-distance 2 of a well-known package. Verify this is the package you meant to install, not a look-alike.
example.source: Curated list of ~165 well-known npm packages, checked via Damerau-Levenshtein edit distance (transpositions, omissions, insertions, substitutions). Not an exhaustive top-N-by-downloads feed.

get.summary: IP reputation check against a curated blocklist
get.description: Checks an IPv4 or IPv6 address against a curated list of netblocks known to be hijacked or controlled by spam/cyber-crime operations. The list copy is refreshed at most once a day; the response includes the list date, attribution and a stale flag if the upstream source has been unreachable long enough for the copy to be over 48 hours old. Free, no signup.

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address to check (IPv4-mapped IPv6 such as ::ffff:1.2.3.4 is checked against the IPv4 list) against a curated list of known hijacked or cyber-crime-controlled netblocks.

list_date.description: Date of the list version used (YYYY-MM-DD)

stale.description: True if the list copy is older than 48 hours (upstream unreachable)

example.source: Spamhaus DROP (Don't Route Or Peer) -- netblocks known to be hijacked or controlled by spam/cyber-crime operations. IPv4 and IPv6 (separate lists). Spamhaus re-evaluates listings daily; this service refreshes its copy at most once a day.
example.note: This IP falls within a netblock Spamhaus lists as entirely controlled by spammers or hijackers.

get.description: Follows a URL's complete redirect chain (up to 15 hops), recording each hop's status and destination -- not just the final URL.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: URL to follow the full redirect chain for, hop by hop.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: GitHub repository in owner/name format, e.g. lodash/lodash.

example.description: A modern JavaScript utility library delivering modularity, performance, & extras.

post.description: Checks up to 20 npm packages in one request, counted as a single request for rate limiting. Same analysis as GET; a missing package yields found=false and a registry failure or invalid entry yields an error field, without failing the batch.

results.description: One entry per input name, in input order. Same fields as the GET response, or {package, error} for an invalid entry.

400.description: Invalid JSON body, unsupported ecosystem, empty list, or more than 20 names

get.summary: Detect a suspicious npm package maintainer change
get.description: Flags a previously unseen human publisher taking over an npm package after 180+ days of inactivity, within the last 365 days -- the pattern behind the event-stream compromise (2018). Older handoffs are counted but not flagged; transitions to npm trusted publishing (verified OIDC identity, not just a bot-like account name) and pre-release versions are reported separately without raising the flag. Does NOT detect a hijacked existing maintainer account (ua-parser-js, 2021) or a malicious release by an existing maintainer (colors.js, 2022). A batch POST variant is available. npm only for now.

parameters.name: ecosystem
parameters.description: Currently only "npm" is supported.

parameters.name: package
parameters.description: Package name, e.g. lodash

200.description: Maintainer change analysis for the package

publisher_check.description: Whether the new publisher's other packages could be looked up. unavailable (e.g. npm search rate limit): the event stays flagged without that check.

trusted_publisher.description: Trusted publishing provider id set by the npm registry (e.g. github, gitlab). Only verified trusted publishing exempts an event; a bot-like account name does not.

established_publisher_events.description: Events whose new publisher already maintains another widely used npm package (100,000+ weekly downloads, excluding this one): most likely a legitimate maintainer handover. Reported, but they do not trigger suspicious.

example.note: Flags a previously unseen human publisher taking over after 180+ days of inactivity, within the last 365 days. New publishers who already maintain another widely used package (100,000+ weekly downloads) are listed under established_publisher_events without triggering suspicious. Heuristic signal for manual review, not proof of compromise. Does not detect a hijacked existing account or a malicious release by an existing maintainer.

get.description: Combines maintainer-change-check (npm only), vulnerability-check, typosquat-check, and repo-health-check (auto-resolved from registry metadata when possible) into a single call with one overall verdict.

parameters.description: Package ecosystem. maintainer-change-check only runs for npm.
